chunks: And do not be like her who untwisted her yarn after it was spun strong, making it loose threads, who made your oaths a means of deceit between you, because one group would be greater than another group; God only tests you with this, and He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection what you used to differ about.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the woman who untwisted her yarn in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the incident of the Banu Murrah and Banu Jadhima tribes, illustrating how tribal loyalty and deceitful oaths led to the unraveling of social cohesion. It serves as a warning against 'fickleness' (nakath) in covenants, emphasizing that breaking promises for temporary gain is a test from Allah that will be clearly revealed on the Day of Judgment.
